A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DnA research and contain 38 complete, readable pages, including supplementary Sections A–C. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image and video experiments in Section 4, plus downstream evaluations, robustness tests and ablations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons, ablations and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same softmax/softmin branches, separate query/value projections, learnable mixing weights and video adaptations.

E1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same training and evaluation coverage across image classification, video understanding, detection, segmentation and distribution-shift benchmarks. No datasets or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including differential and Cog attention in Tables 1–2, the TimeSformer and VisCoP comparisons in Table 3, and parameter-matched ViT-B variants in Table 12.

E3.justification: The training budgets, input resolutions, splits, metrics and evaluation procedures remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix C. Removing percent signs from gain annotations in Tables 11–12 does not change the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same subspace analyses, noise robustness tests, component and parameter-count ablations, attention visualizations, entropy analyses and negative-branch initialization study.

E5.justification: Table 6 retains the same three independent runs and identical uncertainty entries. No repeated-run information, uncertainty estimation procedures or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 1 retains 81.9 versus 81.1 top-1 accuracy for DnA and ViT-B, and Table 3 retains 78.6 versus 78.1 average scores for DnA and VisCoP. Tables 11–12 change gain notation only.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–4, Proposition 1, the optimization formulations and Appendix B's assumptions and proof remain unchanged after matching citation renumbering and text reflow.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about separating positive and negative interactions, denoising attention and improving performance across visual tasks.

C2.justification: The interpretations of subspace separation, noise suppression and ablation results are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same parameter-overhead limitation and proposed future work on parameter efficiency.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, resource measurements and code/project access information are unchanged. The corrected Table 13 cross-reference points to an initialization study already present in v1.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 89 works in corresponding contexts. The relocated Llama 3 entry is the same source; author-name corrections, access dates and added report-institution metadata do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 corrects '§13' to 'Table 13', standardizes some section-reference wording, updates bibliography metadata and adds thanks to Dominick Reilly. The narrative and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 11–12 remove percent signs from absolute-gain annotations, Table 11 changes '% Gain' to 'Gain', and both tables become narrower. There is limited text and bibliography reflow; all figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves navigation and presentation through the corrected Table 13 pointer, more complete bibliography metadata and more consistent absolute-gain labels in Tables 11–12. These are limited editorial gains; the scientific methods, evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
